subject: Recap: per-1M token target & benchmarking for AcmeHealth integration
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: per-1M token target & benchmarking for AcmeHealth integration

Hi Liam — great speaking earlier. Quick recap from our discovery + the pricing notes you asked for. I pulled together a short comparison vs the hosts you mentioned and a draft target bucket for budget planning. Attachments: redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.xlsx (xlsx), comparison_openai_anthropic.csv (csv).

Key points from our call:
- Estimated steady-state volume: 1.2M - 3.5M prompt+completion tokens / day (burst to ~6M/day on weekdays).
- Primary workload: multi-turn clinical summarization + embeddings for search (embedding volume ~10% of token volume).
- Target cost profile (customer target): ~$60 - $120 per 1M tokens (you mentioned "must be < $100/1M ideally").

Benchmark (summary of the CSV):
- OpenAI (gpt-4o/4.1 family): list prices translate to roughly $85 - $140 / 1M tokens depending on completion ratio and streaming vs non-streaming.
- Anthropic (Claude-like): observed range $75 - $130 / 1M tokens for similar seq-length mixes.
- Public self-hosted (quantized open models on managed infra): can be lower ($40 - $90 / 1M) but operational variability and latency tradeoffs are common.

Redwood indicative placement (see attached sheet) — conservative working examples we can offer for procurement review: 
- Standard Hosted: $95 / 1M tokens (includes 30-day SLA, audit logs, and basic export).
- Committed Reserved (3-12 month): $65 / 1M tokens (volume commit required, burst allowed).
- Dedicated Private (on VPC): $55 / 1M tokens + infra pass-through (negotiated).

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm which pricing track you prefer (hosted vs committed vs private).
2) Share target contract length + any minimum monthly spend you can commit to (even rough range helps).
3) If desired, we can run a 2-week proof-of-concept (PoC) with a capped credit to validate latency and quality — we can size that PoC to ~10-20% of expected daily volume.

Questions for you (short):
- Is the $100/1M upper bound a hard stop or a negotiation starting point?
- Any compliance items (e.g., SOC2 audit evidence, data residency) that will drive us toward Private?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick follow-up with procurement if that helps.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
aomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0183

Attachments: redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.xlsx (xlsx), comparison_openai_anthropic.csv (csv)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@acmecorp.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 18:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: per-1M token target & benchmarking for AcmeHealth integration

Naomi — thanks for the clear write-up and the files. A couple quick clarifications from procurement: 
- $100/1M is our internal preferred threshold but we do have flexibility up to $120/1M if the SLA + compliance package is baked in.
- We are strongly leaning towards a committed reserved track (6-12 months) if we can get reliable latency and a pilot that proves the KV caching behavior on our longer sessions.
- Compliance: SOC 2 plus HIPAA addendum required. We have to keep PHI flow rules tight; Private deployment is an option but adds procurement friction.

Action: I can share a redacted copy of our procurement template — procurement@acmecorp.com. Would you and your team be willing to propose a 6-month reserved commit at $70/1M as a starting anchor? If not, what minimal commitments would get you to $70?

— Liam

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>

Naomi / Marissa — quick internal response for negotiation playbook.

Summary: AcmeHealth looking for $70/1M on a 6-month reserved commit with expected monthly average 40-80M tokens. HIPAA + SOC2 in play.

Suggested commercial structure (what will get us to $70):
- Minimum 6-month term, committed spend of at least 1.5B tokens total (250M tokens/month avg). If they cannot commit that high, we can tier discounts with a waterfall schedule: 
  * 0-100M/mo -> $95/1M
  * 100-250M/mo -> $75/1M
  * >250M/mo -> $70/1M (target)
- Upfront 60 days invoice or prepay discount (2.5%) to make the math work on infra capex.
- Add HIPAA addendum + SOC2 evidence as part of Hosted Committed package; if they require Private VPC, add $0.01 per token equivalent infra pass-through that we offset with a lower base rate.
- Include a 4-week PoC credit (~$12K cap) to validate latency/KV caching; PoC must exercise at least 20% of projected throughput.

If Procurement pushes $70 with only a 6-month duration and <200M/mo we should push back and request either: longer term (12 mo), higher spend, or a slightly higher blended rate ($80/1M) with a performance review at month 3.

Operational asks for Solutions/Infra:
- Marissa, confirm whether we can provide the HIPAA addendum in hosted committed within 7 business days and the expected lead time for SOC2 artifact delivery.
- Naomi, if you can share the actual token distribution (prompt vs completion ratio) and sample session lengths, infra can validate whether dedicated KV caching will meet their latency SLO.

I'll stand on next steps in procurement negotiations if you want me to loop legal.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
